newsitem.title: MEXICO: Coke Femsa details quarterly results.
newsitem.headline: Coke Femsa details quarterly results.

text.p: Mexico-based beverage company Coca-Cola Femsa said on Sunday that sales volumes at its Mexico and Argentine units increased during the third quarter compared to the same quarter a year earlier.
The company said in a statement that sales volumes in Mexico grew to 71.5 million unit cases, an increase of 10.9 percent versus the year-ago quarter.
Sales volume in Mexico City, the country's biggest market, rose to 54.2 million unit cases, up 11.7 percent, while volumes in the southeast region grew 8.5 percent to 17.4 million unit cases.

Net revenues at its Mexico unit grew 6.4 percent, lower than the overall growth in volumes due to a 4.1 percent decrease in per unit prices compared to the year-ago quarter, the company said. It did not give the net revenues figure.

Gross profit grew 5.9 percent to 484.8 million pesos. Gross margin fell just 0.2 percentage points to 45 percent despite a higher percentage of sales (up 9.5 percentage points) in non-returnable bottles, which are more expensive, the company said.
Operating profits in the Mexico unit grew to 128.5 million pesos, up 8.5 percent compared to the third quarter of 1995. Operating margin was up 0.2 percentage points to 11.9 percent.

In the company's Argentine business, sales volumes grew 23.6 percent to 23.3 million unit cases compared to the year-ago quarter. Not counting the San Isidro territory added earlier this year, sales volumes grew 9.7 percent.
Net revenues in KOFBA, as the Argentinue unit is known, grew 22.8 percent to 88.2 million Argentine pesos, while cost of sales grew just 12.1 percent.
KOFBA's gross margin grew 5.5 percentage points to 39.3 percent. Operating profits, excluding amortization, grew 10.9 percent to 33.6 million Argentine pesos.
KOFBA's net profit was 1.3 million Argentine pesos, which compares to a 5.7 million loss during last year's third quarter.
KOF, as the company is known at the group level, on Friday reported a nine-month net profit of 227.2 million pesos versus 292.17 million during the year-ago quarter.
Third quarter profits were 100 million pesos, down 0.9 percent versus the year-ago quarter.

Operating profits grew 87.6 percent, including the deduction of amortization of the credit used to buy rights to the San Isidro territory. Operating margin was 7.3 percent, up 2.8 percentage points compared to the year-ago quarter.
Cash flow grew 19.9 percent to 248.9 million pesos.
Integral cost of financing was 12.1 million pesos. Interest expense was up 68.4 percent due to higher debt and less interest income.
